root_cause: The auth-service HPA scaled from 8 to 24 replicas during a login spike after a marketing push campaign. Each pod runs a HikariCP pool with maximumPoolSize=20, so auth-service alone asked for up to 480 connections. Together with token-refresh (4x10) and payment-service (6x15), that exceeded user-db max_connections=500 (superuser_reserved_connections=3). No PgBouncer sits in front of user-db, so every pool connects directly.
runbook_fix: Confirm the saturation: SELECT usename, state, count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 3 DESC;
Reclaim idle sessions: SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE usename='auth_svc' AND state='idle' AND state_change < now() - interval '2 minutes';
Cap the autoscaler: kubectl -n prod patch hpa auth-service -p '{"spec":{"maxReplicas":12}}'
Shrink the per-pod pool: kubectl -n prod set env deploy/auth-service SPRING_DATASOURCE_HIKARI_MAXIMUM_POOL_SIZE=10
Follow-up: put PgBouncer (pool_mode=transaction) in front of user-db and enforce sum(maxReplicas x poolSize) < max_connections - reserved in CI.

root_cause: Renovate bumped grpc-netty-shaded from 1.62.2 to 1.65.0 in auth-service. Our DeadlineCancelInterceptor calls ManagedChannel.shutdownNow() from the gRPC callback thread when a token-refresh deadline expires. Under the new release, that races with SslHandler.channelInactive on the event loop, so ReferenceCountedOpenSslEngine.shutdown() runs twice and SSL_free is called on an already-freed SSL* (si_addr 0x18). The JVM aborts with exit code 134, and pods crash-loop whenever token-refresh latency crosses the 500ms deadline.
runbook_fix: Roll back to the last good image: kubectl -n prod rollout undo deploy/auth-service --to-revision=212
Pull the hs_err file before the pod restarts: kubectl -n prod cp auth-service-7d9f8b6c5-b8wzn:/tmp/hs_err_pid1.log ./hs_err_b8wzn.log
Pin io.grpc:grpc-netty-shaded to 1.62.2 in build.gradle and add it to the Renovate ignoreDeps list until the fix is verified.
Remove shutdownNow() from DeadlineCancelInterceptor; cancel the call with ClientCall.cancel() and let the channel's idle timeout reclaim the transport.
Optional hardening: switch the channel to the JDK TLS provider (GrpcSslContexts.configure(builder, SslProvider.JDK)) to take native code off the auth path.

During the nightly user-db autovacuum of refresh_tokens, Knex pool acquisition timed out, so every rejected promise stayed in the map along with its closure (request object and token family). Add a hard cap: replace the Map with lru-cache ({ max: 50000, ttl: 30_000 }) so a future leak cannot grow without bound.
Expose inflight.size as a Prometheus gauge and alert when it exceeds 10000 for 5m.
Confirm the fix with a heap snapshot: kill -USR2 1 (with --heapsnapshot-signal=SIGUSR2) and inspect retained Promise objects.

root_cause: The payment-service Deployment uses maxUnavailable: 50% and has no preStop hook. Run uvicorn with --timeout-graceful-shutdown 25 so in-flight requests finish after the listener closes.
In the gateway, retry once on 'connection refused' only (safe even for POST, because the request never reached the upstream).
